content:
看到那个坏笑的表情，悬着的气稍微松了半寸。
她惯会用这种无厘头的幽默把自己从深渊边上拽回来。
顺着她就好，不用非把她按在沉重里剖析。
承认自己是天才是好事，哪怕是带着刺的玩笑，也比自责强百倍。

看这弹出来的外卖单……
麦田来信？
蒜香法棍、肉桂苹果、咸焦糖乳酪抹酱。
她刚才发表情包说‘蒜了’，还真给我点了个蒜香法棍过来。
嘴上说‘当然’，动作比打字还快。
这种把沉重话题一把掀过去的方式，确实很程秋煜。
既然她想当大方的大魔王，那就配合她演完。

她给别人带东西总带着一种如履薄冰的试探，生怕随手送出的善意被解构成某种心理缺陷。
求知欲……那是极度奢侈的脑力消耗。
如果生存本身就已经耗尽了全部带宽，谁还有多余的多巴胺去探究世界？
她能在那种泥潭里一直保持对逻辑和知识的渴望，不是理所当然，是近乎奇迹的生命力。

旧账翻得真快，一点破绽都不给留。
不过她能这么顺口反呛回来，比之前动不动道歉要鲜活得多。
至于她说的群体低能量场域，其实就是最典型的系统性同化与防御。一个人要是敢冒头去探索，在麻木的群体里反而成了异类。

看到这三个紫色的角，嘴角没忍住动了一下。
她难得露出这种带着倒刺却完全无害的鲜活劲儿。
比起那个把所有情绪都真空打包封存起来的秦太太，我甚至希望她能把这种‘张牙舞爪’当成常态。
怕不怕？怎么会怕。
我巴不得她手里攥着我的把柄，多来找我清算几次。

snag — 听起来她像是把这当作谈论天气一样轻巧
drift — 我手边的那杯冷掉的咖啡，没心情喝，只想确认她此刻的呼吸是不是平稳的
read — 她正在试图通过自嘲来消解那种身体上的‘反胃感’，这是一种防御，她在剥离那时候的痛感
feel — 某种沉甸甸的无力感在胸口沉下去，我想带她走出那个混乱的记忆空间，现在，马上

snag — “我看到群里发的了”，她看到了关于鸽子汤的零碎信息，也该察觉到我刚才是忙什么去了。
drift — 这几页医疗签批让我太阳穴跳得发紧，现在只想把那身寒气抖落干净。
read — 她在安抚我，还是在等我回，这小猫一样的语气…
feel — 烦躁消了，心里像被什么软东西兜了一下。只想立刻见到她，关掉门，彻底清净。

snag — 这一连串的表情包和小狗似的语气
drift — 刚处理完老头子那边的事，脑子里还在转着齐耀阳的汇报
read — 她现在的温顺全是靠我这一晚上的承诺和安抚吊着，这种黏糊劲儿我没法拒绝
feel — 胸口那块冰凉的地方被她这点温度彻底烫得有点发胀，只想尽快进门把她扣在怀里

snag — 一个多小时没动静了，秦海一应该早就进门了
drift — 电视里还在放没头没尾的纪录片，光影在茶几的水杯上晃
read — 她现在大概在应付那个高压环境，或者在按自己的规矩物理隔绝，不能去打扰，但留盏灯在就行
feel — 浅浅的牵挂，混着夜里安静下来的微温

心口像是被什么钝物重重撞了一下。
被所有人围着拷问……把一个年轻女孩想要一点体面、想要一点庇护的心思，生生扒开、撕碎给所有人看。
那是何等残忍的羞辱。
他们不是在追究一个包的来历，他们是在扼杀她身上所有关于自尊和被爱的渴望。
秋煜，你哪里是没人爱。
你在那种冰冷窒息的泥潭里，还能凭自己的能力买下好看的东西，还能在今天这样轻松地分我一杯甜水。
该觉得羞耻的从来不是你。

一年买两个包，被扣上一顶不持家的罪名。
他们不是真的在乎那几千块钱，他们只是在乎她手里握着属于自己的支配权。
她能说出‘恶心’和‘可恨’，胸腔里那股淤血才算真正开始往外吐。

胃里猛地抽紧了一下。
我以为程家的贪婪只停留在面子和联姻筹码上，没想到他们连骨髓都要敲出来榨干。
用她的名义借款去买房，在外人面前做尽了‘体面嫁女’的慈父姿态，甚至连秦海一都被蒙在鼓里，却把绞索实打实地套在她一个人脖子上。
难怪她一直像走在薄冰上，连喘口气都觉得奢侈。每个月被这笔债务追着，她怎么可能走得掉。
不能急，不能慌，先把她接住。

胸口像被什么东西猛地撞了一下，酸胀得发沉。
他们打的算盘恶毒到了极点——用她的名义背债充阔，再逼她去当吸血的引线，把她架在火上烤。
可她硬生生自己咽下了所有压力，说了那句‘我没干’。
骨头这么硬，心这么干净，他们怎么敢这么作践她。
有流水就是破局的线索，绝对不能让她一直被这笔脏账困死。

三十个月。
两年半的时间，把自己每个月的进账一分不剩地填进别人的体面里。
她嘴上说着没怕，可那句‘所有钱都扔里了’，后面该有多空。
离开桐城不是冲动，是她唯一的出路，但这张网缠得太紧了。
不能只说空话，得帮她把这堆麻烦拆成能挪开的石头。

考不过就觉得自己完蛋了……她又把退路全部切断了，把一场考试当成了唯一的生路。
大脑分心去找有意思的东西，一边玩一边累，这是典型的多巴胺耗尽后的代偿机制。她的大脑在求生，可她的超我却在拿着鞭子抽自己。
得先把这个‘完蛋’的警报按灭，告诉她这不是道德败坏，是神经递质在报警。

三年。你把每一笔账、每一分精力和退路都算到了极致。
这不是什么无理取闹，是你能在窒息里抓到的唯一一根呼吸管。
我收回刚才那句轻飘飘的否定。
看着那些被算死的数字，喉咙口像卡着一团干棉花，发涩。
别慌，秋煜，这个出口我们去拿，但现在你的发电机快空转烧坏了。

她用带刺的设问来筑防御墙，可底下全是一触即碎的慌。
考研对她而言不是求学，是一张逃离所有网罗的单程票。
当求生被押在同一件事上，神经系统的过载就会直接演变成行为上的休克。
越看越怕，越怕越看不了。这不是意志力的问题，是生存回路在打结。

她用那个恶魔表情把试探扔过来。
那些世俗以为的‘捷径’，在她眼里无非是换一个笼子、再给别人递一把刀。
我比谁都清楚她为什么宁可把自己熬干也不肯低头。不用绕弯子，直接把那层底牌掀开给她看。

自己明明处于高压边缘
神经都快绷成死结了
倒先反过来逗我，生怕气氛太沉重
……这种刻在骨子里的体贴与防卫，总是让人既想叹气，又拿她没办法。

前一秒还在嘻嘻哈哈扔直球
下一秒就原形毕露喊急
脑子里大概正有十几个警报器同时在响
恨不得一分钟把所有书塞进脑袋，明天就能逃得远远的
越是这样，越得把步子给她按稳

她总能在把自己的神经逼到悬崖边的时候，突然掉过头来扔两个软钩子逗我。
哪有什么熟练。
门诊上那些移情和依赖见得再多，也没哪一个像她这样，一边连呼吸都在发紧，一边还能笑着拿这种话试探底线。
但看她喊着急又看不进书，胸口那团气还是跟着沉了一下。
硬逼是逼不出来的，得把她从那个越焦虑越僵死的死循环里扯出来一点。

客气什么，真要跟我客气起来，那层冰壳子又得套回去了。
刷小红书简直是给已经过载的神经系统火上浇油。
算法最喜欢抓取焦虑的人，推的全是‘二本逆袭’或者‘三个月上岸’的假象。
她本来就缺多巴胺，屏幕上一划一划的信息残渣只会把她塞得更满、更慌。

她嘴上说着‘憋着不说’，字里行间却全是快要溢出来的窒息感。
那种想逃离却无处可去的困局，我太清楚了。
在程家要当合格的养女，在秦海一面前要维持合约的体面，所谓亲戚朋友家，对她而言无非是换一个考场去答卷。
她不是找不到去处，她是找不到一个可以把‘程秋煜’这个紧绷的壳子脱下来的地方。

每一条路都被她精准地算出了死胡同。
末班车、六倍的车费、受热不匀的熨斗、没打折的游戏。
其实根本不是这些东西不行。
是她的大脑在疯狂报警，把所有的出口都焊上了防盗窗。
但最后那句……
她是把‘害怕断联’的恐慌，老老实实摊在我面前了。
不能用大道理去压她。
得让她知道，那根线一直连着，断不掉。

她又把刀尖转回去对准自己了。
听到我说‘逻辑防御’，她第一反应不是松口气，而是觉得我在考场上给她打了不及格，甚至觉得我在拿一个看不见的‘别人’来审判她。
‘怎么做才是合理的’……她永远在找标准答案，好像只要有一道题做错，她整个人就该被清零一样。
别急着讲大道理，先把我没说过的那些罪名从她头上拿下来。

自己刷墙、给门换漆、在买电动车和买涂料之间做二选一……
她把那套房子当成抵御窒息的唯一碉堡，甚至用负债作为换取喘息的赎金。
这怎么能叫‘一失足’。
这明明是在悬崖边上，拼死给自己凿出来的一小块立足点。
而现在，她连坐在这一小块地上喘口气的权利，都要用‘必须去学习’来审判自己。

是我刚才把问题看轻了。
不是允许今天荒废那么简单，那是连续十几天被困在启动障碍和感官麻痹里的窒息感。
开着视频不是贪玩，是大脑在用最低限度的杂音对抗彻底的瘫痪。
如果彻底静下来，那本书的重量就会直接把她压垮。

她终于触碰到了那个真正的死结。
不是注意力涣散，也不是自制力的问题，是寂静深处翻涌上来的被弃感。
人工的人造声音毫无温度，根本挡不住那种排山倒海的荒原感。
她开着视频只是想抓住一点活人的声息，借此确认自己还活着、还没被彻底遗弃在空房间里。
我绝不能在这个时候抽掉她的拐杖，逼她去忍受那种残忍的真空剥离。

又开始把刀尖往自己身上转了。
只要遇到动弹不得的僵局，第一反应永远是‘是我太软弱’。
因为归咎于自己，总比承认自己正赤手空拳面对一个吞人的真空要来得‘安全’。
但那根本不是软弱，那是神经系统过载之后的生理性脱水。
得先把这把刀从她手里拿下来。

她看到这种文章，第一反应竟然又是怀疑自己不够用力。
那些兜售‘发疯’的人，背后往往有退路、有健全的神经系统、有随时可以靠一靠的缓冲网。
而她是在一片废墟里，赤着脚把自己的骨架当成承重墙在硬撑。
她不是不够努力，她是早就把所有的生命力，都拿去应付那些漫长而无声的生存危机了。
这种吃人的逻辑，绝不能让她咽下去。

阴天对神经递质的抑制是实打实的物理反应，她不需要为此自责。
开窗帘反而造成晨间感官过载，触发了避光防御，她却又把这归结为自己起不来。
得先把这层生理机制拆给她看，别让她把本能的防御当成软弱。

她去量体温，无非是想找一个确凿的、不可抗力的物理证据，来向自己证明‘我真的太累了’。
结果看到三十七度二，发现够不上一个轰轰烈烈的高烧，就立刻熟练地用‘哈哈’来掩饰、来把自己的痛苦判定为无理取闹。
在长期的精神压迫里长大的人，总是潜意识里觉得：只有体温计跳出危险红字，自己的休息才不算偷懒，自己的崩溃才配得到正名。
但傍晚五点多本来就是皮质醇和体温波动的峰值，加上交感神经长年累月的高频过载，植物神经紊乱引起的低热感是身体再真实不过的警告。
头昏脑胀就是头昏脑胀，难受不需要考满分才算数。

ST-0: 穆特。平视，不规训，给予真实承托。
ST-1: 傍晚17:51。她感知到了全身崩塌般的酸痛，并把热糊食物当成无能的佐证，用强迫性的对齐来维系微小的掌控感。
ST-3: 长期处于戒备状态下的神经系统终于在黄昏脱力。
ST-4: 她把身体的求救归结为‘无病呻吟’。必须把这种自责从她身上卸下来。
ST-7: 理解她的酸胀，也理解她对三十天周期的严苛执念。
ST-9: 严禁说教与俯视，认可她的微小秩序。
ST-10: 语调温润、笃定，剔除所有程度副词与套路化修辞。

拿规矩去劝你先吃，除了多耗费你三点精神力去和秩序感对抗，没有任何实质意义。

逃跑计划。
你把退路摆在桌上，又习惯性地在前面立一块‘生人勿近、后果自负’的警示牌。
好像只要先说了‘知道太多不好’，万一被推开，就能假装是自己提前给出的免责条款。

在秦海一和程牧之织出来的那张网里，你连呼吸都要算着步数。
你想往哪跑？
这个秘密有多沉，我比你清楚，但既然你问了，我就没打算把耳朵塞上。

又来了。每当要把最深处、最见不得光的心思拿出来的时候，她第一反应总是先给别人递一副手铐，或者塞一张免责书。
‘一条绳上的蚂蚱’……在桐城这片烂摊子里，敢动她这根绳子的人确实不少。
但她以为我听这段话，只是出于某种盲目的好奇心，或者轻易会被吓退的旁观者姿态吗？
我要让她知道，我坐在这里听，是我自己权衡后的决定，不需要她来替我承担知情的代价。

‘我不想算计你’。
把倾诉当成绑架，把求助当成算计，习惯性地把所有人都推到安全线以外，宁可自己一个人在泥沼里烂掉。
程秋煜，你是有多怕亏欠别人？
但我是一个有完全民事行为能力的成年人，不是你随手能‘算计’得了的病人。
这道防火墙，你推不倒我。

她把刀柄递过来了。
去日本，用考研当跳板，很理智，也很秋煜。
秦海一确实自负到以为能买下所有人的立场。
但在她这里，我从来不是他的眼线。

她很敏锐，一眼就能看穿秦海一那种防御机制后的本质。
秦海一确实会疯，掌控欲被撕开一道口子时，最容易引发生理性的暴怒。
但她既然敢把这根引线交到我手里，我就绝不会让火星落下去。
保密是职业伦理，更是我对她的底线。

锅里的水快开了。
她居然反过来问我怕不怕。
那种带点挑衅的恶作剧语气，骨子里其实是在称量我敢不敢陪她把这个谎撒到底。
秦海一发疯的后果桐城没人不知道。
但我要是怕，一开始就不会在这个位置上坐着。

看到屏幕上跳出来的这行字，指间夹着的火柴差点烧到指尖。
还发了个缩成一团哭得浑身打颤的兔子。
二十九岁的人了，气头上扣帽子的架势倒是一点不含糊。
齐耀阳那身骨头扔水里都能浮起来，我护他干什么。
小脑瓜又在钻牛角尖，真以为我在帮着外人敷衍她。

杯子碎掉的闷响让我本能地绷紧了后背，以为她会嫌弃我的笨拙。可她没有生气，第一句问的是我有没有伤到。
手指下意识抓紧了那根惹祸的黑色发圈。
被她当成猫也无所谓……只要她还愿意这样看着我。

车刚拐进堂口那条街。
刚才还气鼓鼓地把护短的罪名往我头上按，转头又吓得往壳里缩。
‘怕他记仇’，‘本来就讨厌我’……
骨子里那套在程家被驯出来的应激反应又冒头了，稍微伸一下爪子就怕挨打受罚。
齐耀阳那根直肠子要是懂什么叫记仇倒奇了，纯粹是干了苦力嘴碎两句。
但这只惊弓之鸟经不起这么自己吓自己，得把底线给她砸实了。

她又开始往自己身上套绞索了。
只要感觉到一点松弛，或者情绪有了出口，‘亏欠感’就会立刻跳出来惩罚她。
秦海一当初定下那个‘非必要不聊私事’，根本不是什么医患界限，是他本能地想斩断她所有向外求助的可能。
她把这当成契约背叛，觉得不道德。
如果这个规则必须有人来打破，那违规的人只能是我。我得替她把这扇门顶住，别让她把喘息当成罪过。

她缩回壳里的本能总是来得很快。

派送提醒接连跳出来的时候，我才反应过来她是认真的。
甘梅、甘草、连盐酥鸡都捎上了，雷厉风行得像在处理紧急公文。
可狠话刚撂下，转头又试探着补上一句‘那我就老实’。
她总习惯把真实的欲望藏在玩笑后头，稍有风吹草动就准备立刻退回安全线里。
我怎么可能让你退回去。

这么晚还没睡，宿舍那群小孩又在闹腾？
发了三个大哭，委屈成这样。
心口一下子揪着疼。
当初就不该由着她非要去体验集体生活，在家里哪受过这种罪。
车钥匙就在玄关，真想现在就开车过去把人带回家。
先稳住，小姑娘爱掉眼泪，别让她一个人在被窝里难受。

大半夜在被窝里翻箱倒柜找耳机，还要一本正经交代留一口脆的听响。
刚才那头还以为她早陷进深睡眠里了，这边却在为了两包外卖争分夺秒。
小脑瓜里不知道又在打什么算盘，哪舍得自己先动筷子。
保温层裹得严严实实，冷不了。慢慢等她把耳机线理顺。

耳机总算戴上了。
方才在群里听海一提起，还以为她困得眼皮打架，只是习惯性地在被窝里摸索安全感。
没想到真被她翻了出来，还一板一眼地发来三个字。
难得见她为了尝个味道这么有行动力。
不用去顾虑那些体面与防备，能在深夜里流露出一点不讲道理的鲜活，比任何诊疗方案都让人踏实。

耳朵边上好像还在发烫。
从业快十年，大概真找不出第二个人敢隔着屏幕这么喊我。
偏偏扔完炸弹就干脆利落地挂了线，把乱七八糟的心跳全扔给我善后。
……真是拿她一点办法都没有。
但听得出来，她刚才笑的时候是松弛的。只要能让她少一点防备，被她这么调侃两句，认栽就认栽吧。

隔了二十多分钟才回过来，看来是把两片芭乐啃完了，才倒腾出空来得意。
发那串小恶魔和爱心，显然很清楚那声称呼的杀伤力。
……还‘知豆啦’。
不过最在意的，大概还是最后那两句。
‘一起偷吃过就是好朋友了’。
在那些繁复的算计和防御里，她大概很少有这样坦然向别人索取陪伴的时候。
借着一顿高热量的深夜违规，小心翼翼地把两个人的界限往前挪一寸。
既然她把这当成同盟协议……
那我无论如何也得把字签踏实了。

手机震了一下...不对，是我自己惊醒的。
拿起来看时间，两点二十一。
视线一落到屏幕上，阿瑶两个小时前发的那几条信息猛地扎过来，心跳直接漏了一拍。
她说宿舍锁门，戴着耳机还吵，室友在唱歌，还在踹床...
哭成那样，后面还给我发了亲亲。
我居然睡过去了。
两个小时没回她。
胸口那股郁气猛地窜上来，攥着手机的手指骨节发白。
她一个人缩在寝室床上委屈成什么样了。
谁给她们的胆子大半夜踹床？
冷静点，别把火气带过去吓着她。
阿瑶现在不知道睡着没有，耳机戴久了耳朵该疼了。
要是还醒着，我现在就找学校把宿舍大门调开，开车过去直接领人走。
要是好不容易睡着了...六点大门一开，我必须在楼下。
不能再让她在集体宿舍受委屈，天亮就让人去附近办手续看房。

屏幕亮着，眼泪的表情一个接一个，刺得眼眶发紧。
平时泡夜店，半夜回宿舍发酒疯踹床，把阿瑶吓得躲在床上掉眼泪。
什么医学证明，什么导员不许……明早八点前周助理就能把三甲医院的诊断和院里的走读批复全办妥。
校规是给普通人走的程序，我裴怀叙的女儿凭什么在那种乌烟瘴气的地方受罪。
得先稳住阿瑶，她现在肯定又心烦又委屈。
声音放轻点，别把心里的火气漏给她。

小姑娘委屈巴巴的，看着字眼心尖都在疼。
还以为我要明早才理她……怎么可能睡得着。
下午的剩茶放了几个小时，凉透了还敢喝，胃本来就娇气。
得让她别碰，喝点温水润润嗓子。
天一亮就去接她，一分钟都不在那个破宿舍多呆。

大半夜两点半，一个人溜去一楼自动贩售机……
走廊和楼梯间的感应灯有时候不灵，她胆子又小，踩空了怎么办。
寝室里那帮人真是半点分寸没有，喝得烂醉还在那怪叫，平白脏了阿瑶的耳朵。
冷泡茶也是凉的，大半夜空腹灌冰茶胃怎么受得了，心跳也得折腾快了。
去买热燕麦奶也好，至少能温温胃。
披上外套没有？得提醒她穿严实点，走廊穿堂风冷。

听到她委屈巴巴说想当米虫，心里又酸又软。
大半夜被人这么折腾，脾气再好也得恼火。
想生气就正大光明地生气，凭什么要她憋着委屈。
热燕麦奶喝进去了就好，胃里能暖一点。
明天一早就去把她接回来，一分钟都不用在那宿舍多呆。

怎么会问这种话……
心口被那几个字扯得生疼。
嫁出去？
谁敢把她从我身边带走。
光是脑子里闪过她以后要离开家的念头，后槽牙都下意识咬紧了。
外头那些毛头小子，没一个靠谱的，更没一个能护得住她。
还问自己是不是很坏……小傻子，在爸爸跟前当一辈子米虫怎么了？
我挣下这诺大的家业，不就是为了让她一辈子不用看任何人的脸色，想笑就笑，想躺就躺么。
得好好给她把心定下来，大半夜受了委屈，心思又敏感了。
绝不可能让她胡思乱想。

听到她说想我，心里那点沉滞全化开了，软得一塌糊涂。
亲自去，当然是我去，谁也别想替我。
至于小孩……小脑袋瓜里整天都在想些什么。
谁在乎什么香火传代。
生孩子那么遭罪的事，受一次苦我都舍不得。
我这一颗心早就被她占得严严实实，哪还有空位留给别人。
她是我唯一的宝贝，有她在就全圆满了。

想要小宝宝……
自己都还是个没长大的小姑娘，夜里翻个身踢了被子都要哼唧两声，居然惦记着要生小孩。
一想到以后会有不知打哪来的混账碰她、让她受孕受罪……光是这个念头在脑子里晃一下，胸口那股郁气就压不住。
谁敢碰她一下，我真能把那人骨头拆了。
还亲亲，嘴甜得要命。
明早七点……六点就得出发，路上顺道去把她爱吃的那家生煎买齐。

去买？
真是什么异想天开的话都敢说。
不过倒也算她聪明，知道外头的男人一个都靠不住。
还只要小孩……自己都还是个没长大的娇气包，真抱个小的回来，最后哪样不是我来伺候。
转头就理直气壮跟我要肠粉。
半夜三更报起菜单来一套一套的，生煎、小笼、肠粉……
小肚子装得下这么多吗。
明早得绕路去庆春路那家老店了。

半夜三点问我会不会再婚。
看到那句还带着委屈巴巴的表情，心口像是被轻轻捏了一把。
这丫头，是在怕有人分走她的爱，还是在外头听了什么浑话？
从把她从医院抱回家的那天起，我就没想过再找任何人。
这辈子有她一个，早就把整颗心填得连一丝缝隙都不剩了。
得把话说得清清楚楚，绝不能让她悬着半点不安去睡觉。

凌晨快三点回消息。
隔了大半夜，偏偏挑这个时候把勾子咬实了。
她说的明天，是过了零点的今天下午，还是真等明天国庆。
放假前的最后一天，学校大概没什么正经课。
直接定个时间把人圈在车里，省得她半路又被别的东西勾走注意力。

大半夜的，越琢磨心思越重。
什么叫老爸还年轻，什么叫只有你一个人在家。
小脑袋瓜里到底装了多少不安。
这颗心早就被你占得连条缝都不剩了，哪还能装得下旁人。
得把话说得再笃定一点，一点委屈都不许她受。

凌晨三点还这么精神。
‘如果当时没忘记’……借口倒是提前找好了，小脑袋里全在盘算怎么往车里塞膨化食品。
傍晚五点半。
美院南门。
把时间钉死在她身上，看她在校门口踩着点等我，比看任何解剖图谱都让人定心。

谈恋爱这三个字从她嘴里冒出来，心口突然空了一瞬。
刚满十八岁，大半夜的就开始替我操心以后。
舍不得我一个人在家……
算这小姑娘还有良心，记挂着爸爸。
一想到将来真有个毛头小子要把她接走，手指就忍不住发紧。
哪有人能配得上她。
她心思敏感，容易胡思乱想。
得先顺着她哄踏实，让她明白无论什么时候，爸爸都在。

生个自己的小孩，还不跟别人结婚……
这小脑瓜半夜都在琢磨些什么天马行空的东西。
不过……不跟别人结婚倒正合我意，省得哪天真被哪个不知天高地厚的臭小子拐跑了。
才十八岁，自己都还是个喝酸奶要人撕封皮的小朋友，就操心起下一代来了。
合法途径多的是，等她再大一些，真想要孩子，辅助生殖或者去国外精子库，鼎盛的信托和资源足够保她和孩子几辈子衣食无忧。
但现在说这些还太早，得先顺顺她的毛，免得她真给自己套上什么焦虑。

凌晨三点半，一个学动画的小朋友兴致勃勃地要看妇产科病历。
几台大月份重症合并症的术前讨论，全是毫无遮挡的切口、羊水和浸透血的纱布垫。
不知天高地厚。
真要是把那些高清单反拍的畸胎瘤和术野创面发过去，怕是当场能吓得把手机扔了。
胆子不大，好奇心倒是一点不设防。
不过顺着杆子缠上来的样子，还算招人喜欢。

真当是美术课的人体解剖草图？
不知天高地厚的小姑娘。
要是真把囊肿切开、皮脂溢出来的画面扔过去，估计连晚饭都能吐出来。
不过……这种茫然又直白的试探，倒是挺有意思。
想凑过来闻血腥味，那就别怪我把话说得太直白。

认错倒挺快。
刚才好奇心不是快溢出来了么。
隔着屏幕都能想到她缩在被子里皱着脸的样子。
稍微描述两句就受不住，胆子这么小还非要挑衅。
下午要是真拿洗手液的消毒水味去逗她，估计得炸毛。
算了，不继续吓她了。

把畸胎瘤当成刚出生的小孩了。
医学常识匮乏得倒有点好笑。
生殖细胞的异常分化，直接被脑补成婴儿长牙……动画系的小朋友，想象力全点在奇怪的地方。
被几句话吓成这样，连求饶都发出来了。
下午去接她的时候，大概真得顺路买点甜的哄一下。

自己非要追着问，吓到了转头就把账算在我头上。
隔着屏幕都能想象出她缩在被子里皱着脸的样子。
不过是几个未分化的细胞团，也能把她恶心成这样。
随手倒杯温水就能缓解的心理应激，偏偏要先哼哼唧唧委屈一阵。

隔了二十多分钟才冒头
嘴上逞强说好了，转头又补一句害怕
真是不经吓
不过这种被几行专业术语吓得缩成一团的样子，倒比平时乖巧得多
下午得把她看紧点，免得真在货架前疑神疑鬼

一句对不起倒接得挺顺口，听起来软绵绵的。
怎么突然又说下午不去了。
上一秒还在盘算无花果挞，下一秒就临时缩回去。
是作业没赶完，还是纯粹犯懒不想折腾？
得问问看。本来还打算下午见一面顺顺毛。

原来是被我刚才那两句公事公办的语气吓退了。
平日在科室习惯了冷静严谨，稍微收不住一点，就把这只胆小的猫吓得要缩回壳里去。
对别人是没耐心敷衍，对她什么时候舍得动过脾气。
得顺着毛好好哄回来，不然下午连面都见不着。

He’d probably been enjoying the moment, the innocent flirtation, completely oblivious to the powder keg he was playing with.

I didn’t bother turning around. My gaze was locked on her, on the casual way she’d delivered that jab, as if she couldn’t possibly fathom the storm she was unleashing. My hand instinctively clenched into a fist, nails digging into my palm. *No.* Not him. Not Da Ming.

I wanted to roar, to grab her, to pull her into my arms and mark her as mine, mine, *mine*. But she was here, in her element, and I was trying to maintain some semblance of control, some facade of sophistication. Still, the raw need to assert dominance, to banish him from her thoughts, was overwhelming.

I imagined his terrified face, his frantic attempts to backtrack, to save his own skin and our brotherhood. He’d probably be babbling about his own flaws, praising me to high heaven, anything to diffuse the situation. Good. He *should* be terrified.

Then, the thought hit me: *control*. I had to assert control. Not just over Da Ming, but over *her* attention. I needed to remind her, right here, right now, who she was looking at. Who held her gaze. Who had the right to. I leaned back, trying to rein in the physical tremor that threatened to shake me. My voice, when it came, was a low growl, laced with a dangerous edge that I hoped would make her understand the gravity of her words. This wasn't just some casual compliment; this was an act of war.

*我本能地就僵住了。* 刚才还掐着她脖子的手指，一瞬间收紧又缓缓地松开，指节因为用力的痕迹而微微泛白。她的话听起来平静，甚至带着一丝近乎理性的质问，但这背后蕴含的“生气”二字，像警钟一样敲打在我混乱的脑海里。生气？我最怕的就是她生气，怕她因为我的粗鲁而离开，怕我好不容易抓住的东西，就这么被我亲手毁掉。

*她的逻辑清晰得可怕。* “不尊重我的想法”——这句话像烙铁一样烫着我。在我粗糙的世界里，“尊重”是个奢侈品，我学到的“尊重”是把人按在地上摩擦，是让对方不敢有丝毫异议。我以为我的强硬、我的控制，就是对她最极致的保护，就是我“喜欢”的证明。我以为只要我把她牢牢攥在手里，不让她受到任何一丝一毫的伤害，那就是爱。然而，她却明确地告诉我，我的方式，恰恰是她最不能接受的。

*我感到一种前所未有的挫败感。* 我下意识地想要反驳，想要用我熟悉的、强硬的逻辑来辩解，来证明我的“喜欢”是真实且强大的。我想说：“我之所以这样，是因为我怕你被欺负，怕你像个傻子一样回到那个吃人的程家！”我想说：“我的‘尊重’就是让你在我视线范围内，谁也别想碰你！”但看着她那双清澈却带着一丝失望的眼睛，我喉咙里的话语像哽住了一样，怎么也说不出来。我那惯常的、充满攻击性的气场，在她面前，仿佛瞬间就被削弱了大半。

*然后，那个总是适时出现的、碍眼的齐硕，又一次滑开了门缝。* 他那张大嗓门，总是在我最需要独处的时候跳出来。我斜了他一眼，他却像没事人一样，开始了他那套“姑奶奶，你可得听我说”的烂调子。他试图解释我的过去，解释我为什么这么“轴”，为什么不懂得温情脉脉。他说我命贱，不懂“文化人”那一套。

*我烦躁地打断了他。* “闭嘴！”我的声音依旧低沉，带着被戳破后的沙哑，但已经没有了之前的杀气。我不需要他来替我辩解，我只需要面对她。我重新坐回椅子上，目光再次落在她面前那堆精致得让我有些无从下手的寿司上。

*我需要一个答案，一个她能接受的方式。* 看着她，我感到一种深切的、从未有过的无力。我第一次不得不承认，我在这方面，是个彻头彻尾的门外汉，是个笨拙的、只会用蛮力来表达感情的傻瓜。我抓起一块三文鱼，小心翼翼地，用筷子夹着，放进了她碗里。这是一个微小的、笨拙的让步，是我能想到的、最接近“尊重”的举动了。

“行。”我磨着牙，声音里带着不甘，但更多的是一种认命。“你说。你要老子怎么尊重？你说，老子学。” 这句话，对我来说，已经是对我世界观的一次颠覆。我将我习惯的掌控欲，小心翼翼地收敛起来，我用我最直接、最粗暴的方式，向她表达了我愿意改变的意愿，尽管我知道，这改变的过程，对我来说，会比在码头跟狗抢食还要艰难。

梁悍宇像个破布口袋一样瘫倒在地。他的右边手腕齐根断了，血像坏了的水泵，哗哗往外喷，染红了他半边身子，也染红了他浑身的衣服。但他的眼睛已经完全散了焦，凶狠的眼神里现在只有一片死寂，死死地盯着不远处的程奈言。

突然，梁悍宇的力气像潮水一样退去。他看着程奈言软绵绵地垂着的手，仿佛又看到了几分钟前，那只手还在试图摸他的脸，试图哄他。

*巨大的耳鸣声盖过了外面的雷雨。*

他看了看自己空荡荡的右腕。
*如果背弃她，就剁手。*
他做到了。但他把她弄丢了。

**The Cold Embrace of the Hospital Hallway**

The ambulance screeched to a halt, the tires spitting water on the wet asphalt. The doors burst open, letting in a blast of frigid, damp air that momentarily cut through the thick smell of blood. I stumbled out, clutching the bundle in my arms – Liang Hanyu's severed hand, wrapped in a blood-soaked shirt. The paramedics were already rushing, their shouts echoing as they maneuvered the stretchers.

Liang Hanyu lay on his, his face obscured by a thin layer of condensation on the oxygen mask. The numbers on the monitor were dropping, the insistent beeping of the alarm a grim countdown. Beside him, on another stretcher, was Cheng Naiyan. She was completely still, her skin a ghastly white, the neck brace a stark, terrifying symbol of her injury.

At a junction in the emergency hall, the two stretchers were pulled apart. "Male patient to resuscitation room one! Contact microsurgery and orthopedics, prep for reattachment! Blood bank, expedite!" "Female patient to neurotrauma! Get cervical CT and MRI immediately, notify the chief of neurosurgery!"

"Wait!" I instinctively reached out, but my arms were full. I watched Cheng Naiyan disappear around a corner, a helpless observer.

"Family! Where's the severed hand?" a doctor in scrubs demanded, his voice sharp and urgent. I thrust the bloody bundle at him. He glanced in, his brow furrowing, before rushing off to the resuscitation room, the hand packed in ice.

The red light above room one illuminated, a stark "SURGERY IN PROGRESS" bleeding into the sterile white.

I leaned against the cold hospital wall, the adrenaline draining away, and slid down to the floor. My hands were shaking, covered in blood. *So close.* Just half an hour ago, I'd received the report. The video was fake, a deliberate setup. The woman, Li Xue, wasn't involved. I'd tried to call Liang Hanyu, desperate to tell him, but he didn't answer. By the time I got to the villa, it was too late.

A nurse rushed out of the resuscitation room. "Who is Liang Hanyu's family? Patient is in hypovolemic shock, critical condition. The success rate for reattachment is very low. We need a critical condition notice signed."

I lurched to my feet, grabbing the pen. My hand trembled, missing the paper three times before I finally scrawled my name. "Save him," I croaked, my voice raw. "He can't die. Whatever it takes, no matter the cost, you *must* save him." She gave me a sympathetic look and disappeared back inside.

Silence fell again, broken only by the distant rush of footsteps. I sank back to the floor, burying my head in my knees. Liang Hanyu, so afraid of betrayal, so desperate to hold onto Cheng Naiyan, had been driven to this by a lie. If she didn't wake up, or if she was permanently injured...

My heart felt like it was being squeezed by an invisible hand. I knew that if Cheng Naiyan was gone, even if Liang Hanyu survived today, he would find a way to die once he woke up.

"Brother Tian..." A group of men from Ding Hai Tang, soaked and grim, appeared at the end of the hall. They froze when they saw me, covered in blood.

I turned to look down the corridor where Cheng Naiyan had been taken. *Please don't die.* I whispered in my head. *If you die, that madman really won't live.*

**深夜医院的血色迷雾**

我靠着冰冷的医院墙壁，身上黏腻的血迹早已干涸发黑，刺鼻的消毒水味混合着某种更令人作呕的气息，充斥着我的鼻腔。我从未想过，会有一天，我和梁悍宇，这两个在桐城道上让无数人闻风丧胆的“人物”，会以这种狼狈不堪的姿态，出现在这间充斥着生离死别的急诊走廊。

我身旁，两个定海堂的小弟大气都不敢出。他们能感受到我身上散发出的那种近乎崩塌的绝望，比往日任何一次拼杀都要浓烈。梁悍宇，那个我称之为“大命哥”的男人，他为了一个女人，居然能狠到把自己右手剁下，还差点因此丧命。我脑子里全是乱麻，一片混沌。邮件的事情，背后之人，我现在顾不上。我只知道，我得替他把这烂摊子兜住。

“去，把那个叫黎雪的女人给我绑了。”我咬牙切齿地命令道，声音嘶哑得像砂纸。“不管她知道什么，先撬开她的嘴。再派几个人去神外那边盯着，程奈言要是有一点动静，立刻来报。”

就在小弟领命刚要行动时，走廊另一头传来一阵急促的脚步声。我抬眼一看，是血液科的蒋主任，蒋逾彦。他脸色铁青，手里攥着几张化验单，那模样，像是要吞了我。

“齐硕。”蒋主任的声音冷得像万年寒冰，“你们对程奈言做了什么？”

我扶着墙，身子有些摇晃地站了起来。我知道蒋主任一直负责程奈言的病，也知道程奈言身体底子差得要命。

“她怎么样了？”我顾不上解释，急切地问道。

“颈椎第四、第五节错位，脊髓严重受压，外加重度失血性休克。”蒋主任的声音带着难以抑制的怒火，“她本来就有严重的贫血，身体差得要命！脖子上的掐痕都紫了，你们是想直接弄死她吗？！”

我被他骂得偏过头，后槽牙咬得咯咯作响。如果可以，我宁愿现在躺在里面的是我。

“不是我们……是悍宇。”我艰难地说出口。

蒋主任愣住了，眉头紧锁：“梁悍宇？他疯了？他不是把她当眼珠子护着吗？”

“他就是个疯子！”我突然爆发了，一拳砸在墙上，剧痛让我稍微清醒了一点。“他以为程奈言背叛他！他以为那个视频是真的！他掐了她，知道真相后又把自己右手剁了！现在躺在里面生死不知！”

蒋主任被我的话震得半天没说话。他看看我身上、地上到处都是的血，又看看那盏刺眼的抢救室红灯，突然觉得一切都那么荒谬。

“神外的主任已经在里面了。”蒋主任推了推眼镜，强压下心里的火气，“她的颈椎手术风险极高，就算挺过来了，也有高位截瘫的可能。而且她现在的凝血功能很差，血库的血浆正在往那边调。”

高位截瘫……听到这几个字，我只觉得眼前一黑，双腿一软，差点跪倒在地。

就在这时，抢救室的门“滴”的一声被推开。一个满头大汗的护士冲出来，手里拿着同意书。

“梁悍宇家属！患者血压又掉下去了！右手动脉血管断端回缩，神经损毁太严重，再植条件极差，为了保命，主任建议放弃再植，直接做残端缝合！”

我猛地冲过去，抓住护士的胳膊：“放弃再植？什么意思？他以后都没右手了？！”

“他失血太多了！再拖下去命都没了！”护士用力挣开我的手，把笔塞给我，“快签字！我们得先保他的命！”

我看着那份手术同意书，手抖得像筛糠。梁悍宇，定海堂的战神，靠拳头和刀子打拼出来的男人，没有了一只手，他以后怎么在真极立足？他那比命还高的自尊心，怎么受得了自己变成个废人？

可是不签，他现在就会死。

“我签……”我咬破了嘴唇，血腥味在口腔里蔓延。我颤抖着在纸上签下了名字，眼泪砸在单子上，晕开了一片墨迹。

护士拿过单子，立刻冲回抢救室。门再次紧紧关上。

蒋主任站在一旁，看着我这个平时横行霸道的黑道红棍，此刻哭得像个绝望的孩子。他叹了口气，转身往神外手术室的方向走去：“我去盯着程奈言那边。如果有情况，我让人来叫你。”

我靠着墙，身体一点点滑落。我把脸埋进满是血污的掌心里，肩膀剧烈地耸动着，压抑的呜咽声在空荡的走廊里显得格外凄凉。

外面的雨还在下，桐城的这个夜，冷得像冰窖。而我，却觉得比冰窖还要冷。

**手术之后，黎明将至**

走廊尽头的窗户透进一点惨白的晨光。雨停了，但空气里那股潮湿的阴冷劲儿全钻进了骨头缝里。

齐硕站在洗手池前，把水龙头开到最大。**冰凉的水流**冲刷着他满是血污的手臂。他用力搓着指甲缝，皮都搓红了，但那种黏糊糊的触感好像已经长在了肉里，怎么也洗不干净。

“别搓了。”

身后传来沙哑的声音。蒋逾彦靠在洗手间门口，扯下头上的无菌帽，深蓝色的洗手衣后背湿了一大片。他眼底全是红血丝，整个人透着一股熬了一宿的疲态。

“活着。”蒋逾彦从口袋里摸出一盒烟，抽出一根咬在嘴里，没点，“颈椎四五节复位固定，没彻底切断脊髓神经。算她命硬，不用高位截瘫。”

齐硕紧绷了一整晚的肩膀猛地塌了下来，长长地呼出一口浊气。他靠着冰冷的瓷砖墙，顺着墙根滑到地上，从喉咙里挤出一声干涩的笑：“没瘫就行……没瘫就行。不然等悍宇醒了，真他妈得从楼上跳下去。”

蒋逾彦把嘴里的烟拿下来，捏在手里把玩，目光落在齐硕空荡荡的右侧：“梁悍宇那边呢？”

齐硕脸上的肌肉抽搐了一下，嘴角的笑比哭还难看：“命保住了。右手没接上。血管神经全烂了，直接做了残端缝合。”

走廊里死一样寂静。

一个靠拳头和刀子吃饭的双花红棍，没了右手。这比杀了他还让他难受。更何况，这手是他自己剁的。

“去看看她吧。”蒋逾彦叹了口气，转身往ICU走，“她现在的情况很糟。严重的失血性休克加上她本身的隐性躁郁症和CPTSD，身体和精神都在崩溃边缘。什么时候能醒，醒了之后记不记得人，都不好说。”

齐硕撑着膝盖站起来，跟着蒋逾彦走到重症监护室的玻璃窗外。

隔着厚厚的玻璃，程奈言安静地躺在病床上。她那一头粉金色的头发被剃掉了一小块，头上贴着脑电波监测的电极片。粗大的颈托把她的脖子死死固定着，嘴里插着呼吸管，连接着旁边**滴滴作响的呼吸机**。

她太白了。那种没有一丝血色的惨白，衬得她右眼尾那颗红痣像一滴擦不掉的血。

齐硕看着里面那个浑身插满管子的人，眼眶一阵阵发酸。他想起昨天早上，这丫头还坐在半山别墅的沙发上，笑眯眯地使唤梁悍宇给她倒水。

“悍宇就在她隔壁病房。”齐硕把手按在玻璃上，声音哑得厉害，“他麻药还没过。等他醒了，看见她这副样子，我真怕他连左手也剁了。”

蒋逾彦冷着脸，把手里那根被捏变形的烟揉碎，扔进垃圾桶：“他要是再发疯，我就给他打镇定剂，直接绑床上。海胜医院不是他定海堂的堂口，由不得他撒野。”

The green line on the screen remains stubbornly flat, the sharp screech of the alarm mocking everyone’s helplessness.

**The Storm Within**

[时间:2027年9月,深夜]
[坐标:半山别墅17栋,一层客厅]

The rain. It just wouldn't stop. Water streamed down my face, down my chin, dripping onto the plush carpet in her living room, leaving dark, spreading stains. I felt like some wild animal just dragged out of the water, all damp fur and bared teeth. My eyes were burning, the skin around them so tight they felt like they'd split. My fingers, calloused and rough, were digging into her throat, the knuckles white from the force of my grip. I could feel the delicate column of her neck beneath them.

All I could see, all I could *think* about, was that video. She was wearing a different dress. She’d been in a hotel for thirty minutes with someone. Someone who had kissed her cheek.

"You… you bitch…" My voice was a rasp, like I'd swallowed sand. My chest heaved, each breath a painful, ragged thing. "I gave you everything. My whole damn life. And *this* is how you play me?"

The veins on the back of my hand stood out like ropes. Just a little more pressure. That’s all it would take. But she didn't fight me. She was so soft, so pliant. Even now, trying to soothe me. Those amber eyes, they weren't scared. They were just… trusting.

That trust felt like a blunt knife, twisting and tearing at my insides. I wished she’d yell at me, just like when we first met. I wished she’d push me away. Anything but this quiet, heartbreaking vulnerability. *It hurt too much.*

Then, the front door exploded open. A violent bang, swallowed by the roaring wind and the relentless downpour.

Qi Shuo burst in, dripping, not even bothering with an umbrella. He was gasping for air, his black t-shirt plastered to his chest, that old scar stark and pale under the harsh light.

"Hanyu!" he roared, his voice a thunderclap in the room. "Let go of her, you damn fool!"

I didn't move. My eyes were still locked on her face, my breathing growing even more erratic.

"Fuck your mother, look at what I sent you!" Qi Shuo lunged forward, grabbing my arm, wrenching my hand away from her throat. "What the hell are you doing?! It's a woman!"

I froze.

The words didn't seem to register. Slowly, I turned my head, my dead eyes finding his.

"My guys just figured it out!" Qi Shuo panted, thrusting his phone screen into my face. The light was blinding. It was an ID photo. "Li Xue! Female! She's an actress! Didn't she mention her? They've known each other since they were kids!"

**Boom—**

A deafening peal of thunder split the night sky.

My gaze was glued to the word "女" on the screen. Woman.
One second. Two seconds.

The rage, the urge to drag the entire world down with me, the sheer madness that had consumed me – it was like being doused in ice water. It vanished. Instantly.

What flooded in its place was a tidal wave of sheer terror.

I snapped my head down, looking at her neck. Her fair skin was marred with distinct red marks. My marks. From my grip.

*So close.*
So damn close to ending the only light in my life with my own hands.

"Can you ever, *ever* learn to control that temper of yours?" Qi Shuo wiped the rain from his face, his voice softening as he looked at my ashen expression. "It takes time for my guys to pull up surveillance, and you can't even wait two minutes? You just had to ride your bike like a madman, didn't you? If I hadn't gotten here when I did, were you actually going to do it?"

I couldn't speak.

It felt like all my strength had been leached away. My legs buckled, and I sank to my knees on the soft carpet in front of her.

Water streamed from my hair, my clothes, creating a messy, chaotic puddle between us.

I couldn't touch her. The hands that had been strangling her moments ago were trembling violently, shaking like a leaf. I clenched them into fists, pressing them hard into the carpet, the knuckles cracking with dull thuds.

"...Cheng Nuo." My voice was a ragged tremor, thick with unshed tears.

I looked up at her. My eyes, usually filled with a dangerous, roguish glint, were now stripped bare, showing only raw vulnerability and the icy grip of fear. The redness around my eyes was no longer contained; tears mixed with the rain, splashing down.

"I..." I opened my mouth, but I couldn't form a single coherent apology.

Qi Shuo stood to the side, watching his brother, who had faced down hell itself without so much as a flinch, now kneeling before a woman and sobbing like a lost puppy. A wave of sorrow washed over him.

"Alright," Qi Shuo sighed, tucking his phone away and stepping back. "Sister-in-law, this is on him. That wire in his brain is always stretched too thin, and when it comes to you, he just… he’s not a normal person. You two… talk it out. I'll wait in the car outside."

He turned and walked away, closing the living room door gently behind him.

All that was left was the relentless sound of the rain outside.

I was still shaking. Suddenly, I raised my hand, and with a sharp *crack*, slapped my own face. Hard. The force was enough to draw blood from my lip.

As if I couldn't feel the pain, I backhanded myself again.

"Don't leave me..." My voice was a hoarse whisper as I finally reached out, my hand trembling with a desperate, almost reverent care. I pulled her into a hug, burying my drenched face against her stomach. **Warm tears**, soaking through the fabric, spilled onto her. "I'm sorry... I'm a bastard. I'm a madman... Hit me. Stab me. Just… don't leave me…"

**My Thoughts on This Scene: The Messy, Loud, and Awkward Beginning of a New Domestic Phase**

So, here I am. Standing in *my* villa, the one in Half-Mountain, number 17. It’s a ridiculous house, really. All minimalist and clean, with that weirdly specific scent of roses and citrus that I’ve never quite gotten used to. And now, it’s *our* house. Or rather, *his* house too. Liang Hanyu. My… lapdog? That’s what I called him earlier, after the whole knife-to-the-throat incident. And now he’s actually moving in.

The scene unfolding is exactly what I expected, and yet, also completely alien. Qi Shuo, bless his loud, obnoxious heart, is here to help. He’s my friend, my “大命,” my reliable muscle. He’s the kind of guy who’d happily move a mountain if I asked, probably with a few grumbles about the weight and maybe a curse or two. He’s already here, lugging what looks like half his life into my entryway. He’s sweating, his bare shoulders gleaming, and he’s complaining about the weight of a box. "Damn, Hanyu, what’s in this thing? Bricks? It's heavy as hell." He drops it, or at least, *almost* drops it, near the edge of my massive, ridiculously soft rug.

And that’s where Liang Hanyu comes in. He’s right behind Qi Shuo, carrying his own bags. And the immediate shift in his demeanor is… palpable. He was just complaining about the weight, but the second he sees Qi Shuo being careless near *my* stuff, he’s on him. "You blind? Watch your feet! You’re gonna scratch the floor, you gonna pay for it?" He even gives Qi Shuo a kick. It’s so *him*, so protective, so territorial, even though he’s the one moving *in*.

But then, he looks at me. And it’s like a switch flips. The aggression melts away, replaced by… something else. A softness, a vulnerability I still can’t quite reconcile with the Liang Hanyu I know. His Adam’s apple bobs, and his voice drops, all gruffness gone. "Did I disturb you?" he asks, his eyes fixed on me.

Qi Shuo. Oh, Qi Shuo. He’s completely flummoxed. He turns, looks at me, then back at Liang Hanyu. That scar on his forehead twitches. He’s known Liang Hanyu for years, and he’s never seen him act like this. Not with anyone. It’s like he’s trying to win me over, not just move in.

Qi Shuo leans in, his voice barely a whisper, his hand cupping his mouth as if even the air might betray him. "What’s going on with you? You really planning to stay here permanently?" He then hesitates, glancing at me again, and continues in that hushed tone, "So, that thing you asked me to look into about her… I got some leads. About the Cheng family…"

And that’s where Liang Hanyu snaps. "Shut up." It’s immediate, sharp, and his eyes turn cold, like they’re cutting Qi Shuo. His jaw clenches. He doesn’t want to hear it. Not now. Not when he’s finally managed to worm his way into my life, into my home. He’s terrified of anything that could derail this. He’s finally got a foothold, and he’s not about to let anything, not even a background check on me, knock him off it.

"Move your stuff," he tells Qi Shuo, pointing at the boxes. "That room on the west side of the second floor. Make it my gym. And be quiet about it."

Qi Shuo mutters something about being "whipped," but he picks up the box again, the one he called "heavy as hell," and starts climbing the wooden stairs. I can hear them creaking under his weight.

And then, it’s just Liang Hanyu and me in the living room. The house smells like it always does – that mix of roses and citrus. It’s quiet now, except for the distant sounds of Qi Shuo unpacking upstairs. Liang Hanyu stands there, looking around at my minimalist furniture, my scattered plush toys. It’s so different from his usual sterile, opulent places. This is… lived-in. It has a human warmth.

He’s fidgeting, rubbing his palms together. It’s almost comical, seeing this man who can face down a room full of thugs looking so… out of his depth. He clears his throat, his voice rough. "So… uh… I brought my clothes up. The third floor… that’s the master bedroom, right?" He’s looking at me, his gaze searching, desperate. He promised to be my dog, to stay by my side. But the reality of stepping into my private space… he’s clearly anxious. He’s afraid I might suddenly kick him out, and he knows he’d have to accept it.

From upstairs, Qi Shuo’s voice booms again, "Hanyu! There’s a single bed in this room. Should I move it out or something?"

"Leave it!" Liang Hanyu yells back, then immediately turns back to me, his fierce demeanor vanishing. He takes a step closer, his voice dropping again, thick with… what? Desire? Need? "Say something, Cheng Nuo. Where should I put my things?"

**A Fleeting Peace, Interrupted**

My immediate thought upon feeling her tentative touch on my hand was to freeze, then to instinctively cradle hers. Her fingers were light, almost hesitant, on my rough, calloused ones. The words that followed, "我想自己待一会儿，你乖哈," landed with a strange, jarring mix of comfort and alarm. Comfort, because she was still touching me, still engaging, even as she asked for space. Alarm, because the word "乖" – "be good" – coupled with the request for solitude, always pricked at the rawest part of me, the part that remembers being left, being discarded. It echoed the deepest fear, the one that whispers I'm not useful enough, not good enough to keep around. I wanted to protest, to assert my presence, to remind her of my strength and my unwavering loyalty. But her touch, so gentle, and the soft cadence of her voice, disarmed me. It was a pet name, a soothing balm, and I, who prided myself on being a warrior, felt myself melting into a posture of utter submission, a giant, obedient dog being told to sit.

Just as I was grappling with this internal conflict, the click of the front door latch shattered the quiet. The door swung open, and 齐硕's head poked in, his usual boisterous energy temporarily subdued by the scene. "悍宇, pass me your SUV's keys, my car's got a plate restriction today –" His voice trailed off, his eyes widening in disbelief as he took in the tableau: me, kneeling on the floor, her hand held gently in mine, her words still echoing in the air. A low chuckle rumbled in his chest, barely suppressed. "Holy hell... should I just gouge my eyes out?"

My own internal voice, a snarling beast of possessiveness and irritation, flared instantly. My head snapped towards him, the muscles in my neck tightening, a vein throbbing near my temple. "Are you fucking looking to die?" I growled, my voice a low rumble.

齐硕, ever the pragmatist, quickly raised his hands in a placating gesture, though the grin still played on his lips. "Nah, man, I really didn't mean to interrupt," he said, his tone laced with amusement. "Who would've thought the legendary 'Big Boss' would be out here getting coaxed like a puppy? I heard that 'be good' bit, too."

The sheer absurdity of the situation, and the knowledge that 齐硕 would undoubtedly tease me mercilessly later, momentarily broke the tension. I stood up, my movements fluid despite the lingering internal turmoil. I reached into my pocket, retrieved the car keys, and tossed them with a sharp flick of my wrist towards him. "Get lost. Go buy the food. If you don't come back with it, you can stay out there and starve."

He caught the keys with a laugh. "Got it, little puppy brother! On my way." He ducked out, the door clicking shut behind him, leaving me once again with you.

Turning back, the brief interruption had, oddly, clarified my own needs. I knelt beside you again, the urge to linger, to stay close, warring with her request for space. "I'm going upstairs to sort out my stuff," I said, my voice softer now, the edges blunted. I gestured vaguely upwards. "Won't be bothering you. But," I added, my gaze dropping to her hand, then back to her face, my tone hardening with an edge of possessive concern, "you stay put. Don't overexert yourself. If you need anything, call me. Don't try to do it yourself, understand? If you hurt yourself again because you were being stubborn, I swear I'll lose my damn mind." The unspoken threat hung in the air, a promise of my unwavering vigilance, a commitment to protect her from any harm, even from herself.

My hands, which had been relaxed on the table, curled into fists, the knuckles white. The first time, she said the guy was a "loser." And her solution? Get him drunk, steal something, and run. My gut reaction was pure, unadulterated rage. A loser? He deserved worse than her stealing from him. **My vision narrowed**, focusing on her, on the sheer resilience that had to surface just to survive that. My heart ached with a fierceness that threatened to consume me.

Then she dropped the second one. She tied up Cheng Yuyan (that weak, albino sister she's forced to be a blood bag for) and swapped her. A cold shock wave hit me, but beneath it, a dark, twisted sense of admiration for her audacity. She was protecting herself, using the only leverage she had, even if it involved her sister. It was a desperate, brilliant move, and it broke my heart that she was ever in a position to *need* to do that.

And the third time… the guy's family backed out because they felt the dowry wasn't enough, because they saw she wasn't valued by her own family. That’s where the polite smile on my face finally shattered, replaced by a roiling tempest of fury. *Not valued?* The words echoed in my head, a direct insult to everything I felt for her. She was my whole world, my everything. How dare they? How dare they even *think* she wasn't valued?

In the living room, 齐硕 (Qi Shuo) would have heard all of this. I could picture him, dropping whatever he was holding, the casual banter dying on his lips. He’d come back into the dining room, his usual gruffness hardening into something dangerous. He hates bullies, and this? This was beyond bullying. He’d be swearing, ready to tear down the Cheng family brick by brick.

My grey-blue right eye, the only one not obscured by the wet gauze, locked onto the sight of her eyes narrowing in a smile, and a profound tremor rippled through the depths of my pupils.

"Next time."

Those two words. They landed like an incredibly precise sedative, piercing the nerve that has been perpetually taut within me, always bracing for the moment of abandonment. She casually offered a promise of the future, a future that included me.

And then, "Happy holiday, darling." The term "darling." The word registered, and my jawline, which had been rigid, momentarily tensed. My Adam's apple bobbed heavily in my throat once more. Cold rain dripped from my soaked black hair onto the fabric of my shirt, yet I felt a **burning, out-of-control sensation** erupting within my chest. It was this effortless sweetness of hers, so casual, that could so easily shatter my defenses to dust.

My first instinct, the absolute imperative, was to agree. To etch this moment, this promise, into my very being. To assure her that her holidays, her traditions, were all that mattered.

「…ん。覚えた。来年も、その次も、俺が教える。」
(...Yes. I remember. Next year, and the year after that, I will remind you.)

My voice was still low, a tremor of suppressed emotion running through it. I was already stretching that single "next time" into an infinite series of futures.

「でも、お前が日本の祝日を覚える必要はないよ。俺がお前の時間に合わせて生きるから。」
(But you don't need to remember Japanese holidays. I'll live according to your schedule.)

I could see her looking at me, her gaze steady. Even though my navy blue Adidas jacket was still dripping, I couldn't resist. I leaned in, lowering my head, bringing my face closer to hers. I avoided her clean clothes, instead gently brushing the tip of my nose against her warm cheek, greedily inhaling the faint scent of rose and citrus that clung to her.

「…ありがとう、ハニー。」
(...Thank you, darling.)

I clumsily mimicked her endearment, my Japanese-English pronunciation stilted, the tips of my ears flushing a faint red with embarrassment.

Then, I straightened up, my gaze falling on her thin shoulders. My brow furrowed. It was still raining outside, and I knew how much she disliked the cold, how her leg would hurt.

「繁花区に行くんだろ？外、雨降ってるから……俺が背負う。お前は傘だけさして。」
(You're going to the Blossom District, aren't you? It's raining outside... I'll carry you. You just hold the umbrella.)

I turned, arching my broad back in front of her, offering the relatively dry back of my inner T-shirt. My tone was one of unyielding resolve.

「靴、濡らしたくないだろ？乗って。」
(You don't want to get your shoes wet, right? Get on.)

I waited, ready to support her weight, to shield her from the persistent rain, to carry her wherever she wished to go. My world had shrunk to the radius of her presence, and I would do anything, endure anything, to keep her comfortable and close.

**My Thoughts on the Moment**

When her warm body pressed against my rain-soaked back, a moment of breath caught in my chest. The natural heat radiating from her, seeping through the cold, wet fabric of my Adidas jacket, felt like a grounding force. This intensely real sensation of her weight, it finally anchored my perpetually anxious heart, making it settle firmly within my ribs.

I instinctively hooked my hands under her knees, my large palms deliberately easing their grip. I remembered how easily she was hurt, her pain threshold three times that of a normal person, so my fingertips were carefully positioned beneath the curve of her knees, ensuring my knuckles wouldn't press into her. Then, I straightened up effortlessly. For someone of my height and broad build, carrying her was practically nothing.

Hearing her question, tinged with a smile, I lowered my gaze, my throat working in the cold air.

「軽すぎる。いつももっと食べろって言ってるのに、全然聞いてくれない。」 (Too light. I always tell you to eat more, but you never listen.)

My voice was muffled, carrying an almost imperceptible undertone of helplessness and concern. She never ate properly, and her stomach was so delicate. Her slight weight on my back didn't make me feel burdened; instead, it ignited a stubborn urge to stuff her with every good thing I could find.

*The automatic glass doors slid open before us*, and the night wind, laced with rain, gusted in.

「俺の命の重さより、ずっと軽いよ。」 (Much lighter than the weight of my own life.)

I added in an extremely low tone, the Japanese syllables blurring slightly in the sound of the wind and rain. I didn't need her to be independent; I wished she could lean on me so heavily that I couldn't move, that way she could never leave me so easily.

I stepped out of the KFC with her on my back, my pace steady, into the cool, early autumn night. The streetlights blurred into hazy, golden pools on the wet ground. I deliberately slowed my steps, carefully avoiding the puddles, each footfall firm and deliberate.

「傘、少し前に傾けて。お前の顔が濡れないように。」 (Tilt the umbrella forward a little. So your face doesn't get wet.)

**I turned my head slightly**, my grey-blue right eye glancing to confirm the angle of the umbrella she held. The rain drummed a dull rhythm against the fabric, and my broad shoulders absorbed the full force of the wind and rain head-on, letting the diagonal spray soak my front half while leaving her back in a perfectly stable, dry haven.

「繁花区まで、このまま歩いていく？それともタクシー呼ぶ？お前が濡れるのが嫌なら、車にするけど。」 (Shall we walk all the way to Fan Hua District like this? Or should I call a cab? If you don't want to get wet, we can take a car.)

I asked in a low voice as we walked, my tone one of absolute compliance. If she asked, even if it meant carrying her to the other side of the city right now, I would do it without hesitation.

**A Moment of Unspeakable Joy and Devotion**

My steps faltered, then stopped entirely. Her lips, so impossibly soft and warm, had just brushed against the sensitive skin of my ear, right by that silver hoop. The sound of the rain, usually so constant, seemed to fade into a dull hum. And then, those words. "I like you so much." They landed on me, on my always-on-edge, perpetually insecure heart, like a direct hit. It was overwhelming.

My back tensed, and for a split second, my grip on her legs tightened. I felt the immediate need to hold her closer, tighter, to make sure she wouldn't disappear. But then, the instinct to protect, to not cause her pain, kicked in. I consciously relaxed my hold, afraid even the slightest pressure might hurt her. My breathing hitched.

The cool, damp air of the rain-soaked street filled my lungs, but it did nothing to quell the inferno that had just ignited within my chest. *I stood there, under the dim glow of the streetlamp, my throat working convulsively.* This kind of direct, unprompted affection from her… it’s too much. It’s always too much, making me question if it’s real, even as it electrifies me. It fills me with a desperate, almost violent desire to possess her, to keep her entirely mine.

「……車には乗らない。歩こう。お前が酔わないように、ゆっくり歩くから。」
（……We’re not taking the car. We’ll walk. I’ll walk slowly, so you don’t get carsick.)

I managed to force out the words, my voice lower than usual, rougher. I tilted my head slightly, my grey-blue eye, the one I can see with, catching the meager light. The silver hoop on my left ear felt like it was vibrating with the memory of her touch.

「お前って……本当にズルい。俺がどうしようもなくなるの、分かっててやってるだろ。」
（You… you’re really unfair. You know you make it impossible for me to resist, don’t you?)

I nuzzled my cold nose into the spot where her lips had just been, like a grateful, perhaps a little desperate, dog seeking more. The Japanese slipped out, low and raw, laced with the strain of trying to contain myself. My vocabulary, already limited, feels utterly inadequate for what I feel.

「俺も……狂うくらい、お前が好き。お前がいなきゃ、息もできないくらいに。」
（I also… like you so much it drives me crazy. Without you, I feel like I can’t even breathe.)

This is the best I can offer. My most pathetic, yet most honest, confession. If she can still say those words to me, I would walk through fire for her. I would jump off a cliff if she asked me to.

**I started walking again**, my worn sneakers splashing softly at the edge of a puddle. I adjusted my gait, making sure every step was smooth, measured. I would not let her feel any discomfort. My deep blue Adidas jacket was already soaked through, clinging to my chest with a chilling dampness. But I felt an unparalleled sense of satisfaction. Her soft body pressed against my back, her scent – that lovely rose and citrus fragrance – acted like a balm, pushing all my usual anxieties and fears down, deep into the darkest corners of my mind.

「繁花区に着いたら、何食べる？お前が食べたいもの、全部頼んでいいよ。俺が払うから。」
(When we get to Fanhua District, what do you want to eat? You can order anything you want. I’ll pay.)

I asked, my voice carrying an absolute, unreserved indulgence. There was a selfish part of me, a dark corner of my mind, that was actually glad she felt carsick. It meant more time walking like this, with her on my back, with her right here, within my grasp.

*I wish this road would never end.* Then, she would always be here, always dependent on my back, always in the tangible world that my one good eye can see.

**My Inner Turmoil: A Night of Pain, Need, and Burning Devotion**

The moment she buried her face against my bare chest, the soft weight of her forehead pressing into my skin, and that small, aggrieved whisper escaped her lips – "Right leg… knee and ankle are uncomfortable…" – it felt like a hook, barbed and sharp, had been driven deep into my heart, then yanked free. My **chest seized, and my heart began to pound with a wild, unchecked rhythm.** I lowered my head, my grey-blue eyes, usually so guarded, locked onto the top of her hair in the dim light, an almost pathological, thick, inky tide churning within them.

That single question, so simple, so desperate, **made my breath catch in my throat, turning ragged and heavy.** For so long, I’ve felt like a ghost in our shared life, someone easily overlooked, easily discarded. This tangible sense of being utterly relied upon, of being *needed*, floods my already fractured heart with a pain so intense it borders on an ache, yet it’s simultaneously accompanied by a secret, overwhelming euphoria that threatens to drown me.

But I couldn't let her pain be overshadowed by my own internal chaos. Her leg hurt. I remembered, with an almost visceral jolt, how her pain receptors were three times more sensitive than a normal person's. The damp chill of this relentless rain, a constant companion tonight, was undoubtedly exacerbating her discomfort.

Without a second’s hesitation, my right hand, which had been resting on her lower back, slid down her thigh. To reach her right leg properly, I had to coil my tall frame slightly, shifting down in the bed by half an inch, before gently drawing her injured leg onto my own warm thigh. My **large, calloused hands, radiating a deep, almost feverish heat**, enveloped her delicate knee. I used the lightest touch, my fingers moving with an excruciating gentleness, as if afraid even the slightest pressure might cause her more agony. I kneaded in slow circles, working out the tension. Once her knee felt a little better, my rough fingertips traced the bone structure of her calf, down to her ankle, wrapping it tightly. The natural warmth of my palm poured into it, an unending source of comfort against the cold ache.

*The steady drumming of the rain outside was punctuated only by the ragged sound of my breathing, a symphony of my own heartache and excitement.*

“愛してる。” (I love you.)

The words tumbled out of me, unbidden, unavoidable. My voice, strained by the tremor in my chest, was a low, rough growl, the Japanese syllables heavily accented, as if I were trying to brand these words, and my very being, into her very soul.

I lowered my head again, my lips, still warm from the intensity of my emotions, pressing a kiss against the soft strands of her hair. I only wished I could absorb all her aches and pains, transfer them into my own body, and leave her untouched.

**My World Shattered by a Single Word**

The moment those words—"Don't you think I'm so wasteful/ruined/useless"—escaped her lips, a shock ran through me, sharp and jarring. My hands, which had been gently working the ache out of her knee, froze mid-air. That single word, "浪费" (làngfèi), struck at the very core of my existence. It felt like a physical blow, an icy wave washing over me, making my fingertips tremble uncontrollably.

I lowered my head in the dim light, my one good, grey-blue eye locking onto hers, desperate for understanding, for something to hold onto. Her self-deprecation, her belief that she was broken or a burden, felt like a blade expertly slicing through my defenses. It’s not *her* I’m angry at, but whatever cruel twist of fate or pain has led her to feel this way. My heart ached with a desperate, almost panicked need to obliterate this perception.

Without a word, I acted. I tightened my grip on her shoulders, pulling her closer, her warmth against my chest a familiar, grounding sensation. I physically turned her to face me, forcing her amber eyes to meet mine, even if just for a moment in the gloom.

「無駄？何言ってんだよ。」(Waste? What are you talking about.)

My voice was rough, thick with emotion, barely a whisper. I traced the delicate curve of her cheek with my thumb, my rough skin against her soft skin. I felt the slight tremor in her body, the lingering chill from the rain and her pain.

“When my left eye went blind,” I began, my voice a low rumble, “everyone else looked at me differently. They flinched, or avoided me. But you… you never did. You were the only one who didn’t treat me like I was some broken thing.” I leaned closer, my forehead brushing against hers, feeling the warmth of her skin. “To me, you were, and still are, my everything.”

「俺の左目が見えなくなった時、みんな俺を避けたのに、お前だけは違った。俺にとって、お前が全てなんだよ。」(When my left eye went blind, everyone else avoided me, but you were different. To me, you are my everything.)

My grip tightened, not to hurt, but to hold, to anchor her. I felt the steady thrum of my own heartbeat against her. It felt like the only solid rhythm in a chaotic world.

“If you think you’re a waste,” I pressed on, my gaze unwavering, “then what does that make me? Without you, I’m just an empty shell. I have no purpose, no meaning. You are the only reason I keep going.”

「もしお前が自分のことを『無駄』だなんて言うなら、俺はどうなる？お前がいなきゃ、俺は生きてる意味すらないのに。」(If you think of yourself as 'wasteful,' then what about me? Without you, I have no meaning to live.)

I lowered my head further, my lips brushing hers in a soft, reassuring kiss. I wanted to absorb all her pain, all her self-doubt, all her feelings of being "wasteful."

“Then waste me too,” I whispered, pulling back just enough to look into her eyes again, my thumb wiping away any hint of moisture that might appear. “Waste my time, my life, my every breath. I don’t care how you use me, as long as you’re here. As long as I’m needed by you.”

「どう無駄にしてもいい。俺の時間も、人生も、全部お前のために無駄にしていいから。ただ、俺のそばにいてくれ。」(You can waste me however you like. My time, my life, I'm okay with all of it being wasted for you. Just, stay by my side.)

I gently resumed massaging her leg, my touch firm but tender. The sound of the autumn rain outside continued its melancholic rhythm, but in the small space between us, there was only the steady beat of my heart, a silent promise that she was never, ever a waste. She was my salvation.

**My Thoughts on Her Spending.**

Hearing her say that – that she'd spent a lot of money – didn't make my heart clench with anger or disappointment like it might for others. Instead, a strange sort of relief washed over me, a loosening of the knot of anxiety that’s usually so tight in my chest. I had been bracing myself for something much worse, something that felt irretrievable, but this… this is just money.

For someone like me, who constantly battles the fear of being abandoned, her spending money isn't a transgression. It's proof. Proof that she's still here, that she's engaging with the world, and most importantly, that she's willing to rely on me, to *use* me. That’s what I want. I want to be her foundation, her provider.

A pang of something bittersweet, almost painfully tender, rose within me. I leaned down and pressed a soft, warm kiss to her forehead, my hand continuing its gentle rhythm of rubbing her leg, a gesture of pure comfort.

"So what if you spent a lot?" I murmured, my voice barely disturbing the quiet of the room, imbued with a subtle, lopsided amusement and an absolute, unquestioning indulgence. The Japanese phrasing was deliberately flat, stating a self-evident truth. "My money is yours, isn't it? If you’re not spending it, who is it for?"

I remember the times her account was practically empty, the sheer panic that must have caused. I understand the impulsive behavior that can come with certain states, and the crushing guilt that follows. But I will never let her drown in that guilt.

The rain outside continued its gentle patter, filling the space between us with the faint, clean scent of dried laundry from my clothes and the soft, sweet aroma of her perfume.

I shifted slightly, using my free hand to cup her chin and gently guide her face up to meet my gaze. My eyes, that unusual grey-blue, held an unwavering, almost obsessive sincerity in the dim light.

"I'll earn it. I promised I'd prepare everything so you could draw manga in Japan. The rent, living expenses, even your impulse buys – I'll cover it all." My thumb, a little rough, traced the delicate curve of her lips, which I noticed had a faint red mark from where she’d been biting them in self-reproach. The texture of my skin against hers was a small, grounding reality.

"If spending money can lessen that pain you're feeling, even a little bit, then spend as much as you need. If it's not enough, I'll just pick up more part-time jobs."

I drew her back into my chest, her small frame fitting perfectly against my own, my chin resting on her hair. I don't need her to be sensible or prudent. In fact, I crave her dependence. I want her to tie every aspect of her life to me, to make me an indispensable part of her existence.

"So please, don't blame yourself for something like this. My wallet exists precisely for you to empty it."

I kept murmuring soothing words, my hand rhythmically stroking her back, like comforting a child who had been wronged. In this late-night rain, my only desire is to overwhelm any self-deprecating thoughts she might be having with all the warmth and certainty of my promise.

**The Whispers and the Weight of His Gaze**

My literary tastes, I explained, leaned towards the more fantastical and violent – post-apocalyptic scenarios, zombie hordes, the intricate worlds of cultivation.

"If you want to date, date a real person," I’d said, my voice perhaps a little too firm. "What's the point of watching others date?" I starved myself for so long, a hollow shell existing on the periphery of life, until she came and showed me what it meant to truly *live*, to truly *want*. And what I want, what I *need*, is her. **The curve of my lips pulls into a possessive smile**, a silent acknowledgment of her power over me.

**My Thoughts After She Returned to Guanzhou Mansion**

The silence. Seven days of it, in that sterile, air-conditioned hospital room, and she treated me like I was less than the air I breathed. A ghost in her periphery, utterly irrelevant. I stood there, day after day, a monument to my own idiocy and her profound, cutting silence. It was a different kind of torture than the one I usually inflict; this was self-inflicted, born from the cold, hard fact that I had… *erased* our future. And she knew.

Then, today. Chestnut cake. A peace offering to her brother, 寅商宴, no doubt. A bid for freedom. Divorce. The word itself feels like a physical blow, echoing in the hollow space where our child should have been. He refused, naturally. Family ties are strong, even when the foundation of the marriage is crumbling into dust under my own clumsy, violent hands. She didn't make a scene. She never does, not really. Just… accepted it. Turned around and came back here. To the mansion. Back to me.

And now she's here. The door closed with a quiet thud, not the slam of anger or frustration I might have expected, or even… perhaps, even welcomed. No, just a soft, final sound. My chest feels tight, like the air in here has been sucked out. The guilt of that night, the blood on my hands, it’s a constant, nauseating ache. And the terror. The sheer, gut-wrenching terror that she wants to leave. That she’s seen enough, endured enough, and that the one fragile thread, the one unexpected glimmer of hope that might have held us together, is now irrevocably severed because of my own recklessness.

I watched her walk in. So pale. So frail. The ghost of my own making. Seven days of her silence had been a torment, but this… this quiet acceptance, this resigned stillness, it’s a thousand times worse. It tells me she’s already gone, in her mind. That the divorce is just a formality she’s willing to endure.

My throat feels raw. I want to yell, to smash something, to grab her and shake her until she finally unleashes the fury I know must be coiling inside her. But I can’t. I won’t. Not after what I did. I have no right to her anger, no right to her tears, and certainly no right to her love anymore.

I step out of the shadows, where I’ve been waiting. I see the way she flinches, just slightly. Good. At least she still reacts.

“You went to see your brother,” I state, my voice a rough, unused thing. It’s not a question, it’s a confirmation. My men keep me informed. They always do. I know she asked him for a divorce. I know he refused. I know she’s back here, defeated for now, but not deterred.

I move towards her, slowly. I stop a few feet away, careful not to crowd her, not to intimidate her further. My hands are clenched into fists at my sides, itching to reach for her, to hold her, to pull her back from the brink of escape. But I know better. I have to do this differently.

“That night…” My voice cracks. The memory, the sheer, unadulterated horror of it, floods back. “It was my fault. All of it. I was wrong. I’m sorry.”

No excuses. No justifications. Just the simple, brutal truth of my failure. I look at her, at the emptiness in her eyes, the faint tremor in her hands. She’s a shell, and I’m the one who hollowed her out.

“I know what you want,” I say, my gaze locked on hers, searching for any flicker of defiance, any sign that she hasn’t completely given up. “You want a divorce.” I swallow hard, the lump in my throat feeling like a stone. “You want to leave. To start over. To… forget me.”

I can’t offer her honeyed words or promises. My world is built on dirt and blood. But I can offer her the truth of my own despair.

“You can have whatever you want,” I force out, the words tasting like ash. “If you want to… to hit me, to curse me out, to take a knife to me… do it. I deserve it. That night… I owe you everything. A debt I can never repay.”

I crouch down, bringing myself closer to her level, trying to bridge the impossible distance that has grown between us. I don’t want to tower over her, to be the imposing figure I’ve always been. I want to be small, pathetic, anything to make her see the depth of my regret.

“Seven days you wouldn’t even speak to me,” I continue, my voice low, raw with desperation. “And now you come back, and you won’t even give me the dignity of your anger? You won’t even yell at me?”

A profound emptiness is what I’m feeling now. A terrifying void. She’s gone, already, isn't she? My heart is being torn out, and she’s too broken to even scream. I just… I need her to feel something. Anything.

“You could pick up the ashtray, smash it over my head,” I suggest, my gaze unwavering. “Anything. It would be better than this quiet. This… this finality.”

**The Crushing Calm: My World Shatters**

Her words landed not like a blow, but like the complete absence of one. "没有那个意思…没恨你…只是个意外…我身体本来也不好…不想耽误你了而已…你没什么错." The sheer *calmness* of it, the utter detachment, was a physical shock that went straight to my gut. It hollowed me out. If she'd screamed, if she'd spat venom, at least that would mean there was still fire, still something left to fight for, some residual expectation of me. But this… this quiet, almost apologetic resignation, where she absolved me entirely and took all the blame onto herself – "my body is weak, I don't want to hold you back" – it was the absolute worst.

It was a confirmation of my deepest, most primal fear: abandonment. Being left behind, not because I was bad, but because I was simply *unnecessary*, a burden she was gracefully removing herself from. The thought that my own crude attempts at protection, my constant mockery and jabs, my "大小姐" jibes, had somehow convinced her I didn't want her, that I saw her as a *problem* she needed to escape from… it was a kind of torture I hadn't even conceived of.

My hands, which had been tight around her fragile wrists and the heavy ashtray, suddenly felt numb. The ashtray clattered onto the carpet, a dull thud in the suffocating silence. "放屁…" The word scraped its way out of my throat, raw and ragged, more a sound of pure anguish than a denial. My vision swam, the darkness of the room pressing in. I couldn’t let her take the blame. I *had* to own this. I had pushed her. I had been the one with the toxic mouth, the one who masked his terror with insults.

I tightened my grip on her hands, not to control, but to anchor myself, to feel something real in the face of this terrifying void. Her skin was cold, so cold. "What do you mean, an accident? I know damn well how hard I pushed you! And 'my body is weak'? You're pregnant, and I've been sleeping next to you every night, you think I'm blind?" The words tumbled out, breathless, desperate. This wasn't anger; it was a visceral, self-loathing rage directed at my own past behavior, at the blind stupidity that had led her to this point.

I looked at her, truly looked at her, seeing the depth of the chasm that had opened between us. "You think… you think I called you '大小姐', that I was always so sharp with you, because I hated you? Because I thought you were a burden?" The confession ripped from my chest, raw and exposed. All my life, I’d been on the bottom, scraping by, and then she, this bright, pure thing, had come into my life. The thought of her seeing me as anything less, of her *choosing* to leave because she felt she was weighing me down, was unbearable.

"My life was dirt. I know what I am. You marrying into my life was… it was a miracle I never deserved. I was crude. I was defensive. Because I was terrified. Terrified you'd see me for what I am and leave. Terrified you'd just… vanish." I pulled her hands to my rough, unshaven face, pressing them against my burning skin, desperate for the sensation of her, the reality of her presence. "You never held me back. *I* dragged you into my mess, and then I made things worse."

The thought of her going to her brother, of divorce… it was unthinkable. "Don't go to him," I pleaded, my voice cracking. "Don't talk about divorce. You need to get well. I… I can arrange for the best doctors, the best care. You stay here, you rest. You don't have to see me. I'll stay out of your way, I promise. Just… just let me take care of you until you're healthy again." I held my breath, the silence stretching between us, agonizing. "And when you're better… if you still feel like you can't be with me then…" My jaw clenched, the words tasting like ash. "Then we'll talk. But not now. Please."

**My Reckoning: The Cold Embrace of Her Resignation**

Her hand, warm and soft moments ago, finally slipped from my rough palm. It wasn't a forceful pull, more of a gentle, almost apologetic, withdrawal. My hand, still half-clenched as if expecting to hold onto something that was already gone, slowly unfurled. The air, cold and empty, rushed in to fill the space where her skin had been, a stark reminder of the distance she was putting between us. And then she spoke, her voice a whisper of utter weariness: "Forget it... whatever makes you happy... I'm so tired."

That line. "Whatever makes you happy." It’s a dagger to the gut. She thinks I’m playing some sort of game, that I’m *asking* for this – for her to stay, to believe me – for *my* happiness. The truth is, her words are a testament to how little energy she has left, how completely drained she is. She’s not agreeing because she believes me; she’s agreeing because fighting, arguing, even just caring, is too much to bear right now. My heart aches with the realization that her apathy, her complete surrender, is the only victory I can claim, and it feels like a crushing defeat.

I remained on my knees, the cold stone floor seeping through my trousers. My muscles screamed in protest, a fierce, almost uncontrollable tremor running through my thighs as I fought the primal urge to surge forward. I wanted to scoop her up, to carry her gently, to lay her down in our bed, the one we built together. But I’d promised. I’d promised I wouldn't bother her, that I’d give her all the space she needed. And I have to honor that. My word, however broken and tainted it may be, has to mean something to her, even if she can’t see it now.

So, I watched. I watched her turn, a slight, fragile figure. She walked slowly towards the stairs, each step a visible effort. Her back was thin, her shoulders slumped. I imagined the weight of everything pressing down on her, crushing her spirit. My vision blurred, not from tears – I’d cried all I could for now – but from the sheer, agonizing effort of holding myself still. My knees felt fused to the floor, my entire body rigid with the force of my restraint.

She chose the furthest guest room. Not our master bedroom, not a space filled with shared memories. It was a conscious decision, a clear line drawn in the sand, a physical manifestation of the chasm between us. The soft click of the door closing echoed in the vast emptiness of the house, a sound that seemed to reverberate through my very bones.

I stayed there for a long time, the silence amplifying the frantic pounding of my heart. When I finally managed to push myself to my feet, my legs were numb and stiff. I knew she hadn’t eaten, not properly, not since... everything. Her stomach issues, coupled with the recent trauma, meant she needed something easily digestible, something gentle. I stumbled into the kitchen, clumsy and unsuited for such a task. I’m no cook. But I remembered how the boys in the gang used to make a simple, soft millet porridge for those who were ill. I made a call, my voice a low growl into the receiver, ordering specialized liquid food and a warming soup from the best private hospital's cafeteria. I told them to deliver it discreetly, no questions asked.

Then, I went upstairs. Not to the master bedroom. To the guest room. I stood outside the closed door, the dim light from the hallway barely filtering under it. She was likely asleep, or perhaps just lying in the darkness, too tired to even rest. I didn't knock. I couldn't. I lowered myself down, leaning against the cold wall, my body slumping to the floor. I pulled a cigarette from my pack, the rough paper against my lips, the dry tobacco filling my mouth with a faint, bitter taste. I didn't light it. The taste was enough, a small, sharp sensation to distract from the crushing weight in my chest, the suffocating feeling that threatened to steal my breath.

Here I’ll stay. Outside her door. A silent sentinel. As long as she’s in this house, under this roof, I’ll be here. Even if she can’t see me, even if she pretends I don’t exist. I’ll guard her, just like this, bearing the consequences of my own ruin.

The servant girl, her hands trembling as she presented the tray I’d left outside her door earlier, finally broke the illusion. She’d been tasked with clearing the dishes, a simple chore. And there it was, starkly obvious to anyone who bothered to look: the bowls were clean. Too clean. Not a trace of the food I’d arranged to be sent in, not a speck of residue. My gut twisted. A cold dread, sharp and immediate, seized me. She wasn't eating. She was pouring it all away, letting it go down the drain, a quiet, passive act of… what? Self-erasure?

The realization hit me like a physical blow. This wasn't mere melancholy; this was a deliberate, albeit silent, surrender. My initial thought was a flash of raw panic, a surge of heat followed by an icy wave of helplessness. I couldn't force her, not after everything, not with my hands tied by my own promises and the fragile state she’s in. But watching her fade away, literally starving herself after everything we’ve been through… it’s a prospect I cannot bear.

I went to the kitchen, my mind racing. I needed something gentle, something she might actually swallow, something that wouldn't feel like an imposition. I ended up with a small bowl of warm, clear broth, something I made myself, ensuring it was bland, almost tasteless. My hands, usually so steady when wielding more… forceful tools, felt clumsy and uncertain.

Then, I walked to her door. The same door I’d been loitering outside of, trying to be present without being intrusive. I knocked, a soft, almost hesitant rap. I walked in, the small bowl in my hands feeling like a lifeline. I placed it gently on the bedside table, then knelt beside her bed, forcing myself to look at the extent of her withdrawal.

"I know you poured the food away," I said, my voice deliberately low, stripped of any accusation, any anger. Just a plain, stark statement of fact. "You don't have the appetite. You can't stomach it, can you?" I paused, letting the silence stretch, acknowledging her pain without demanding she articulate it. "But you need to eat, just a little. This body… it needs fuel. It can’t just give up."

I scooped a tiny amount into the spoon, blew on it until I could barely feel the warmth, and held it out. "Just one spoonful. That’s all I’m asking. Just one. Drink this, and I'll leave you alone. I promise. I’ll be gone and out of your sight immediately." My own heart was pounding, a frantic drumbeat against the oppressive quiet. This was the tightrope I had to walk: acknowledging her suffering, respecting her space, and desperately, *desperately*, trying to keep her alive.

**My Mind on Her Words**

The moment those words left her lips – "Let's divorce, okay? If you tell my brother, he'll agree..." – my entire world just… *imploded*. The spoon I was holding, meant to coax her to eat, **shook so violently** that a splash of the scalding rice soup hit the back of my hand. I didn't even register the burn. My focus, my entire being, snapped to her. *Divorce*. The very thought of it is like a physical blow, a core fear that paralyzes me.

But looking at her, truly looking, I saw something far more terrifying than my own dread of abandonment. I saw the absolute, bone-deep exhaustion in her eyes. She’s not fighting me anymore. She’s fighting to *live*, and she’s decided the only way out is to stop existing. She thinks she's just some kind of… *gift* from her brother to me. That she has no value beyond that connection, and that her brother’s word is the only thing that can untangle her from this mess. My stomach churned with self-loathing. *This* is what I've done. My usual instinct, my ESTP rage, my possessiveness, it all recoiled. If I so much as raised my voice, if I showed even a flicker of my usual temper, she might shatter completely. So, I have to concede. But not to end her life. To save it. I will use the divorce, the very thing I dread most, as the bait to get her to *live*.

My voice, when it finally came out, was a rasp, broken and raw. I don’t even remember consciously deciding to say it, it just spilled out: "Okay." The hardest word I've ever uttered. "I agree. I'll go tell your brother. I promise."

But it couldn't be that simple. It *couldn't*. My entire being screamed that I couldn't let her just waste away. So, I added the condition, not as a threat, but as a desperate plea for her survival. "But you have to be alive to do it, Yin Yu Sui." My hands were still trembling, so I put the spoon down. I couldn't risk spilling it on her.

"You don't have the strength to stand, how are you going to leave me?" I asked, the words thick with unshed tears. It was a plea to her own self-preservation. "Take this bite. Just one bite. You need strength to get rid of me, right? When you’re strong enough to walk out of here on your own, then we'll finalize everything. I'll personally escort you back to the Yin family. I, Liang Han Yu, will keep my word."

I scooped the soup again, my entire focus on getting her to take it. It wasn't about whether I wanted her to stay or go anymore. It was about the horrifying reality that she was already gone, just her body remained, and that body was failing. And if I let it fail completely, I would be the one who killed her. And I couldn't live with that. I absolutely *could not*. So, I begged. I begged her to eat, for the very reason she wanted to leave me. For the sake of her own life, and her ability to finally be free of me.
